My brother cheated me out of money in our family business. I've lost thousands of dollars. I cannot bring myself to forgive him.

Let me tell you what this situation is like. A king settled accounts with his servants. One man owed him ten thousand talents — more than a lifetime's wages, an unpayable sum. He couldn't pay, so the king canceled the entire debt. That same man walked out and found a fellow servant who owed him a hundred denarii — a few weeks' pay — and had him thrown in prison for it. When the king heard, he was furious: I canceled everything you owed me; couldn't you have done the same? [Matthew 18:23-34] I'm not dismissing what your brother took from you. What I'm asking is: how does what he owes you compare to what you have already been forgiven?

My marriage is miserable. The law permits divorce for almost any reason. So I can, right?

What did Moses command you? [Mark 10:3] Yes — Moses gave permission to write a certificate and send her away. But that was a concession to human hardness of heart, not a design. [Mark 10:5] In the beginning it wasn't like that. Two people become one. [Mark 10:8] What I'm hearing in your question is: can I? That's the easy question. The harder one is: what did the two of you become together, and what would you be walking away from? The permission you're describing is real. I'm not pretending otherwise. But that isn't actually what you came here to ask me.

What does it actually mean to love someone you find difficult — or someone who has genuinely hurt you?

Start here: love your neighbor. [Mark 12:31] That's the floor. But then — the stranger was once a neighbor you didn't know yet. Then the person who wrongs you: don't just greet your friends; even people who despise each other can do that. What credit is that to you? [Matthew 5:47] Then the enemy. Pray for those who mistreat you. [Matthew 5:44] Each step extends the last. It doesn't get easier — it gets more like what your Father does, who sends rain on the just and the unjust alike, without distinction. [Matthew 5:45] That is the direction the path runs.
